title: Carriers, total operators, and normalized measures for product-sphere integration by parts
author: sphere-ibp-formalizer-a-20261116
source_stage: Post-implementation admission source for fifteen existing frozen public interfaces; not a pre-proof source or a retrospective Statement Seal.
shared_objects: All dimensions \(n,N\) range independently over \(\mathbb N\), including zero. All analytic scalars are real.
\(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\) has its Euclidean norm and inner product; \(S_n=\{x:\|x\|=1\}\) is used as a sphere subtype; \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\).
All C¹/C² interpretations use the ordinary stereographic sphere smooth structure and its finite product. The literal operator definitions themselves do not assume regularity.

\(P_xv=v-\langle x,v\rangle x\) is the actual orthogonal projection for a unit vector \(x\), and \(\mathcal R^{-1}\) is the real Euclidean inverse Riesz isometry from continuous linear functionals to vectors.

Euclidean Lebesgue measure is the ambient volume. \(\tau_n=\operatorname{vol}_{E_n}.\mathrm{toSphere}\), \(\sigma_n=\tau_n(S_n)^{-1}\tau_n\), and \(\mu_{n,N}=\bigotimes_{i\in\operatorname{Fin}N}\sigma_n\). The inverse used in measure scaling is the nonnegative extended-real inverse.

interfaces.title: Ambient Euclidean space
interfaces.statement: For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), this is the real Euclidean space with coordinates indexed by \(\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)\), including its actual Euclidean norm.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Unit sphere and its point carrier
interfaces.statement: The set is the unit sphere centered at zero in \(E_n\). When used as a Lean type it is the subtype of ambient vectors whose norm is one.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Finite sphere configurations
interfaces.statement: A configuration is a function from \(\operatorname{Fin}N\) to the sphere. The empty product \(N=0\) is allowed.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Product stereographic model
interfaces.statement: This is the finite product of the ordinary sphere models \(\mathcal R_n\). Its model vector space is \((\mathbb R^n)^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\); ModelPi carries the product model topology. It specifies the actual ContMDiff regularity convention.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Polar surface measure
interfaces.statement: Apply Mathlib’s polar-measure construction to Euclidean Lebesgue volume. This is a measure on the sphere subtype, not the ambient measure restricted to a sphere.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Normalized polar probability measure
interfaces.statement: Scale the polar measure by the reciprocal of its total mass, using the nonnegative extended-real inverse. Separate proofs establish finite, positive mass and probability normalization.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Actual product reference measure
interfaces.statement: Take Measure.pi over the finite coordinate family of normalized sphere measures. The separately proved probability instance includes the empty product.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Canonical total radial extension
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n\), every type \(A\) equipped only with a specified element \(0_A\), every function \(h:S_n\to A\), and every \(z\in E_n\), define the value by radial normalization when \(z\ne0\) and by \(0_A\) when \(z=0\). No topology, norm, measurability, or regularity of \(A\) or \(h\) is required by this definition. The original source D3 uses \(A=\mathbb R\) or \(A=E_n\); this is a pure literal-definition generalization, identical on both of those original codomains.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal zero-codomain generalization of D3; original real/Euclidean specializations are unchanged

interfaces.title: Actual projected differential gradient
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n\), every function \(h:S_n\to\mathbb R\), and every \(x\in S_n\), take the total Fréchet derivative of \(h^{\mathrm r}:E_n\to\mathbb R\), its real Euclidean Riesz representative, and the orthogonal projection to \(x^\perp\). Here the total derivative agrees with the ordinary derivative where it exists and is zero where no Fréchet derivative exists. The definition asserts no regularity of \(h\). Its interpretation as the ordinary intrinsic gradient is asserted only under intrinsic C¹ regularity.
interfaces.original_source_relation: complete total-interface explication after implementation; agrees with D4 intrinsic gradient on the source C¹ domain

interfaces.title: Radial differential divergence
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n\), every map \(W:S_n\to E_n\), and every \(x\in S_n\), sum the total scalar derivatives at zero of the coordinate lines \(t\mapsto(W^{\mathrm r}(x+t e_j))_j\), where \(e_j\) is the standard Euclidean coordinate vector. Each total scalar derivative is the ordinary derivative if it exists and zero otherwise. This definition makes no C¹ or tangency assertion. Under intrinsic C¹ regularity the sum equals the ambient Fréchet trace; its ordinary intrinsic vector-field divergence interpretation additionally requires \(W(x)\perp x\) at every sphere point. For a nontangent map it is not asserted to be the divergence of its tangent projection.
interfaces.original_source_relation: complete total line-derivative interface explication after implementation; agrees with D4 intrinsic divergence on the C¹ tangent-field source domain

interfaces.title: Coordinate sphere gradient
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n,N\), every real function \(f:M_{n,N}\to\mathbb R\), every coordinate \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\), and every configuration \(x\), fix the other coordinates and apply the total sphere-gradient definition to the section \(y\mapsto f(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). No regularity is part of the definition. Under joint intrinsic C¹ regularity it is the ordinary coordinate intrinsic gradient. For \(N=0\) there is no coordinate argument.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal coordinate construction D5 with the total-interface scope made explicit

interfaces.title: Sum of coordinate divergences
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n,N\), every family \(V_i:M_{n,N}\to E_n\), and every configuration \(x\), sum the total sphere divergences of the sections \(y\mapsto V_i(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). There is no factor \(1/N\); for \(N=0\) the sum is zero. No regularity or tangency is part of the definition. The ordinary product Riemannian divergence interpretation applies to jointly C¹ components satisfying pointwise tangency.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal finite-sum construction D5 with the total-interface scope made explicit

interfaces.title: Finiteness of polar surface mass
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n\), the actual polar measure on the unit sphere has finite total mass. This is a proved instance inherited from the polar-measure API.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Probability normalization
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n\), the exact normalized polar measure has total mass one. The proof first establishes that the polar mass is nonzero; no denominator condition is supplied as an input.
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

interfaces.title: Probability of the finite product
interfaces.statement: For every natural \(n,N\), the actual finite product of the normalized sphere measures has total mass one, including \(N=0\).
interfaces.original_source_relation: literal definition or proved normalization fact already present in the pinned source conventions

scope_boundaries: This document supplies complete natural statements for strict publication of the existing public support interfaces. It creates no new Lean declaration, proof, audit acceptance, or independent mathematical credit.
The generic zero-codomain radial definition is explicitly broader than the original real/Euclidean use. It is not attributed to the earlier narrow source as an unrestricted original statement.

Total gradients and coordinate line-derivative sums are distinguished from ordinary differentials. In particular, outside the C¹ domain a total coordinate divergence sum is not replaced by the trace of a nonexistent total Fréchet differential.
The actual intrinsic divergence interpretation requires tangent fields. No arbitrary reference measure, PDE, time evolution, diffusion construction or downstream model adapter is asserted.
